session: 2026-09-12, SO-101 follower pick-and-place (brick -> tin), Abderrehmen Gharsallah

field_legend.objective: what the step was trying to achieve

decisions.objective: Inventory the hardware and software before touching the arm.
decisions.inputs: Connected repo folder; lerobot 0.6.2 in a uv venv; the sandbox shell showed no USB devices (isolated Linux VM on the Mac).
decisions.constraints: No direct USB or serial access from the agent sandbox; nothing may move yet.
decisions.decision: Have the user run a scan script in a macOS Terminal that writes serial ports, USB tree, camera list, calibration files and camera snapshots into the repo, which the agent can read.
decisions.action: Wrote outputs/env_scan/scan_hardware.sh; user ran it; report parsed.
decisions.alternatives: Ask the user to type device names manually (error-prone); attempt USB from the sandbox (impossible).
decisions.expected_outcome: Serial port, camera indices and calibration state known without any motion.
decisions.result: Port /dev/cu.usbmodem5A460836731; cameras: index 0 top, 1 wrist, 2 FaceTime, 3 OBS virtual; calibration my_follower exists (Sept 6).

decisions.objective: Control the arm in real time from the agent despite having no hardware access.
decisions.inputs: Shared repo folder is readable/writable by both sides; lerobot SOFollower API (send_action, get_observation).
decisions.constraints: Slow, non-brusque motion; hard joint limits; emergency stop must be independent of the agent; the daemon must be the only bus owner.
decisions.decision: A file-based bridge daemon owns the arm: agent writes JSON goals, daemon interpolates at a capped rate, clamps to limits, streams state.json and camera snapshots.
decisions.action: Wrote outputs/bridge/bridge.py (v1): 30 Hz loop, rate-limited interpolation (default 12 deg/s, max 30), calibration-derived soft limits with 3 deg margin, motor Acceleration=15 and Goal_Velocity=300 caps, lerobot max_relative_target=5 as second guard, ESTOP file, torque kept on at Ctrl-C.
decisions.alternatives: Direct lerobot CLI teleop (needs a leader arm, none present); scripting one-off Python moves per step (no persistent guards, slower loop).
decisions.expected_outcome: Any command, even a wrong one, results in a slow bounded move; user can freeze the arm at any moment.
decisions.result: Worked; became the platform for everything after.

decisions.objective: Recover from a Feetech bus error ('no status packet' writing Lock on motor 2) during connect.
decisions.inputs: Handshake pinged all motors; failure occurred in torque re-enable with zero retries.
decisions.constraints: Must not leave torque half-enabled; must distinguish flakiness from a hardware fault.
decisions.decision: Treat as known Feetech packet loss: retry the connect sequence up to 5 times and use num_retry on setup writes; escalate to hardware check only if all attempts fail.
decisions.action: Patched bridge with a connect retry loop and enable_torque(num_retry=5).
decisions.alternatives: Ask user to re-seat cables immediately (premature); lower baud (unnecessary).
decisions.expected_outcome: Connect succeeds on retry; identical failure 5x would indicate cabling/power.

decisions.objective: Stop an unintended 2-3 deg drift at startup.
decisions.inputs: Rest pose (lift -45.7, elbow 83.2) lies just outside the 3 deg-margin limits; hold command was being clamped, pulling joints toward the limits.
decisions.constraints: A hold must never move the arm.
decisions.decision: Apply limits only to received goals, never to the hold pose.
decisions.action: Removed the clamp from the hold/interpolation path; restart.
decisions.alternatives: Widen margins (would hide the logic error).
decisions.expected_outcome: Startup and hold produce zero motion.

decisions.objective: Prove the command chain and speed limiting with zero risk.
decisions.inputs: Arm at rest; wrist_roll changes nothing about the gripper's position in space.
decisions.constraints: First motion must be harmless and observable.
decisions.decision: Move only wrist_roll +10 deg at 8 deg/s and back.
decisions.action: Sent the goal; measured ~1.3 s for 10 deg.
decisions.alternatives: Start with shoulder/elbow (would change position before the chain was validated).
decisions.expected_outcome: Requested rate observed, no other joint moves.

decisions.objective: Understand why the elbow ignored goals while other joints tracked.
decisions.inputs: Registers identical across motors; Goal_Position accepted; Present_Load only ~18% at 43 ticks of error; user confirmed nothing mechanically blocking.
decisions.constraints: No forcing; test hypotheses one at a time with reversible register writes.
decisions.decision: Rule out the position-limit hypothesis (widen Max_Position_Limit: no effect), then conclude lerobot's P=16 gain is too weak for small steps against gravity and raise the gain.
decisions.action: Wrote P_Coefficient 32 (later 48) to the elbow, 32 to other arm joints; baked into bridge startup.
decisions.alternatives: Larger commanded errors (causes jerks when the motor finally moves); re-calibration (would invalidate all recorded poses).
decisions.result: Moved immediately at P=32; ~2 deg residual sag; 1.5 deg at P=48.

decisions.objective: Bring the gripper above the brick looking straight down.
decisions.inputs: Wrist camera view; discovered signs: lift+ = down/back, elbow- = forward/up, wrist- = view forward, pan+ = scene left.
decisions.constraints: Steps <= 6 deg at 3-5 deg/s; inspect both cameras after each step.
decisions.decision: Learn each joint's effect from one small test move each, then compose moves.
decisions.action: Sequence of single/dual-joint relative steps; reached READY (lift 0, elbow 70.5, wrist 37.5) with the brick centred.
decisions.alternatives: Compute inverse kinematics up front (no reliable link/offset data for this calibration).
decisions.expected_outcome: Brick centred between the jaws in the wrist image.
decisions.result: Achieved; pan alignment learned as ~50 px per 3 deg at that height.

decisions.inputs: Brick apparent size in the wrist image as a height proxy; a 12 deg elbow/wrist step near the table.
decisions.decision: (Mistaken) trust the image-size height estimate and take a larger step to speed up.
decisions.action: Sent elbow +12 / wrist -12; gripper reached the table and kept pressing; user hit Ctrl-C.
decisions.alternatives: Smaller steps with user confirmation of height (adopted afterwards).
decisions.expected_outcome: Tips a few cm above the brick.
decisions.result: FAILURE: table contact. Lessons: image size is not a reliable height cue near the surface; position lag and motor load do not reveal downward pushing (gravity-assisted).

decisions.objective: Give the user instant stop controls and add automatic contact guards.
decisions.inputs: User request for quick stop buttons; incident D08.
decisions.constraints: Stop must work even if the agent is unresponsive; guards must not depend on the camera.
decisions.decision: Add double-clickable STOP/RESUME/RELEASE .command files (ESTOP file mechanism), a stall guard (lag > 4 deg for 0.7 s), a per-joint load guard, a 12 deg step cap, and require user confirmation for each descent step.
decisions.action: Implemented; restart without interrupting torque (skipped lerobot configure()).
decisions.alternatives: Rely on lerobot's max_relative_target alone (does not detect contact).
decisions.expected_outcome: Any resistance freezes the arm; user can freeze it in one click.
decisions.result: Guards work for lateral/upward resistance; downward pushing later proved undetectable this way (see D15).

decisions.objective: Close the gripper on the brick.
decisions.inputs: User confirmed jaw tips beside the brick near the table; wrist image showed the brick between the jaws.
decisions.constraints: Gripper torque capped at 50%; do not crush.
decisions.decision: Command gripper to 10 at 15 units/s and accept the stall position as the grasp indicator.
decisions.alternatives: Close to a computed width (unknown calibration of gripper units).
decisions.result: Held; 20.4 became the reference value for grasp verification.

decisions.objective: Lift the brick above the tin rim and release it inside.
decisions.inputs: Top camera for position over the tin; user directions ('4 cm forward', 'slightly right').
decisions.constraints: Clear the ~5.5 cm rim; the wrist camera's view is offset from the jaws, so trust the top camera and the user for XY.
decisions.decision: Lift with shoulder_lift -10 (twice), move with pan, then adjust with elbow-/lift+ pairs for level forward motion; ask the user to confirm before opening.
decisions.action: Reached pan 6.8 / lift 26.5 / elbow 47.7 / wrist 5; opened gripper; brick landed in the tin.
decisions.alternatives: Vision-guided drop using the wrist camera alone (parallax made it misleading).
decisions.expected_outcome: Brick visible inside the tin in the wrist image.
decisions.result: SUCCESS (first pick-and-place, human-in-the-loop). The load-guard threshold tripped once on normal elbow gravity load and was made per-joint.

decisions.objective: Provide a live stream and a one-button autonomous routine.
decisions.inputs: All poses from the manual run; HSV analysis of saved frames for the yellow brick.
decisions.constraints: Same guards for every control path; stream must not add load to the control loop.
decisions.decision: Add an HTTP dashboard (MJPEG of both cameras with detection overlay, state, STOP/RESUME/HOLD/AUTO/ABORT/RELEASE) and a routine that replays waypoints with a wrist-camera pan servo and an image-size stop criterion.
decisions.alternatives: Pure waypoint replay without vision (brick position had already changed by ~4 cm).
decisions.expected_outcome: User can watch live and start/stop the routine; routine reproduces the manual run.
decisions.result: Two failures: fragmented detection in dim light (fixed by merging blobs, lower gates) and fixed waypoints unable to reach a farther brick (led to D14).

decisions.objective: Let the user demonstrate motions and define poses instead of the agent guessing.
decisions.inputs: User request for joint controls and real-time saving of moves.
decisions.constraints: Same limits and guards apply to manual jogging; free-drive must be explicit and confirmed.
decisions.decision: Add per-joint sliders/step buttons, REC (10 Hz jsonl), named waypoints with Go, FREE-DRIVE/ENGAGE, GO TO REST, configurable rest pose (rest.json), and limits.json 'extend' to widen a joint range with matching motor register updates.
decisions.action: Implemented; shoulder_lift range widened to [-47, 98] after the user measured 101 deg by hand; user saved a new rest pose.
decisions.alternatives: Re-run lerobot calibration to widen the sweep (would shift all joint zeros and invalidate recorded poses).
decisions.expected_outcome: User can jog, record and define poses; the arm can reach farther forward.
decisions.result: Used successfully; the extended shoulder range was essential for the later autonomous grasps.

decisions.objective: Make the approach adaptive to the brick's position.
decisions.inputs: Wrist detection (x, y, size); learned joint effects.
decisions.constraints: Small steps, guards active, detections may drop out for a frame.
decisions.decision: Replace fixed descent waypoints with a visual-servo loop: pan <- brick x, elbow <- brick y (reach), shoulder <- height, wrist compensating to keep looking down; wait up to 2 s for detections.
decisions.action: Deployed v3; ran under agent supervision.
decisions.alternatives: User demonstration replay only (does not generalise to a moved brick).
decisions.expected_outcome: Brick centred and at grasp size regardless of start position.
decisions.result: Alignment converged, but the height cue (image size) collapsed when the close-up brick washed out; the loop kept descending and touched the table; user pressed STOP (see D15).

decisions.objective: Know the fingertip height from joint angles, independent of the camera.
decisions.inputs: User proposal to teach table-contact poses; 5 contact poses provided by free-drive plus 2 observed contacts; SO-101 link lengths.
decisions.constraints: Guard must never let goals go below the table; model must be honest about extrapolation.
decisions.decision: Fit a planar 3-link kinematic chain (joint offsets, axis signs, shoulder height) so all taught contacts have height 0; use it to clamp goals (>= 8 mm), freeze on negative height, and drive the descent to a 1 cm target. Offline tests showed a measured shoulder height makes the fit exact; without it the model is accurate near the table but not in the folded region.
decisions.action: Implemented FloorModel, Mark-contact button with contact height, floor_config.json anchor; fit rms 1.4 mm on 7 points.
decisions.alternatives: Surface regression contact_lift = f(elbow, wrist) (poor extrapolation); force sensing (not available; loads are uninformative when pushing down).
decisions.expected_outcome: Descent stops at ~1 cm predicted tip height; no table contact.
decisions.result: Both subsequent autonomous runs stopped at 1.3-1.4 cm and grasped.

decisions.objective: Keep the brick detected at all distances and lighting.
decisions.inputs: HSV samples: brick hue 17-24, saturation 45-145 (drops when close/washed out), table saturation <= 33, tin label orange hue ~15 ring-shaped.
decisions.constraints: Never let a detection artefact drive a motion decision toward the table.
decisions.decision: Gate hue 14-40, sat >= 40, val >= 80; open(5)+close(21) to merge stud columns; solidity/fill filters; treat a > 40% size collapse as a bad reading; wait for detections at routine start.
decisions.alternatives: Fixed high saturation gate (fragmented the brick); learned detector (unnecessary for one known object).
decisions.expected_outcome: Whole brick boxed in both views; size cue used only as a sanity check.
decisions.result: No detection-caused failures in the final two runs.

decisions.objective: Pick the brick and place it in the tin with no human input.
decisions.inputs: Floor model, visual servo, gripper stall check, proven carry/drop/retreat poses, configured rest pose.
decisions.constraints: 4 deg/s near objects; abort and freeze on any guard, lost brick, missed grasp; 1 s pause before release for a human STOP.
decisions.decision: Run the routine end to end under agent log supervision.
decisions.action: Run 1 (18:27): servo 9 iterations, grasp at 1.3 cm, size 351 px, stall 20.4, released, rest. Run 2 (18:31) from a different brick position: 10 iterations, 1.4 cm, 367 px, stall 20.4, released, rest.
decisions.alternatives: Continue human-in-the-loop (already validated; goal was autonomy).
decisions.expected_outcome: Log shows 'AUTO: done'; wrist image shows the brick inside the tin.

decisions.objective: Preserve everything needed for a smaller model or a person to repeat this safely.
decisions.inputs: Whole session: quirks, conventions, thresholds, poses, run outcomes.
decisions.constraints: Literal, step-by-step; machine-readable numbers; failure -> remedy mapping.
decisions.decision: Write LEARNINGS.md (why), README.md (how, schemas, procedures, remedies), metadata.json (all numbers), this decision log, and propose a reusable skill.
decisions.action: Files written to outputs/bridge/ on the Mac.
decisions.alternatives: Rely on the chat transcript (not accessible to other sessions or models).
decisions.expected_outcome: A new operator can start the bridge, run AUTO PICK and recover from every known failure without rediscovery.
decisions.result: Delivered; note outputs/ is git-ignored (user to decide on tracking).

cross_cutting_lessons: Validate the command chain with a harmless joint before any positional move.
Learn each joint's sign with a single small step and a camera check; write the conventions down.
Image-based height estimates are unreliable near the surface; use a geometric model anchored by taught contacts (and a measured shoulder height).
Motor load and position lag do not reveal downward pushing on a gravity-assisted axis.
Detection dropouts are normal: wait/retry before declaring an object lost; treat abrupt size collapses as errors.
Servo gains from lerobot defaults (P=16) can be too weak for small smooth steps; verify tracking before trusting 'reached'.
Never interrupt torque on reconnect while holding an object; skip library configure() steps that do.
Every control path (human, agent, routine) must share the same limits and guards.
Keep the human in the loop with one-click stop and confirmations for the first instance of any risky move; automate only what has been demonstrated safe.
